_readme: WHAT EVERY BRANCH SHARES. scripts/harness/branch-sync.js reads this file and checks one thing per
entry. On the SOURCE BRANCH (the repo's default branch, detected — see the script's header) it
checks that every listed path exists and every probe holds; on any other branch it checks that
every listed path is byte-identical to the source's — and it reads THIS FILE FROM THE SOURCE REF,
never from the branch under test, so a branch cannot exempt itself by editing its own copy.
files       compared whole.
dirs        mirrored exactly: the same file set, every file byte-identical. A file the source no
longer has is drift too, which is how a deleted harness helper stops lingering on an
old branch and going on being loaded there.
perBranch   deliberately NOT compared; only their existence is checked. These are the files that
say what THIS branch is, or hold figures measured HERE.
sections    compared with one `## ` section masked, so a branch can say what it is in one section
of AGENTS.md while the rest of that file stays common. `except` is a heading PREFIX.
ignore      .gitignore is per-branch and its order matters, so its EFFECT is probed instead, with
`git check-ignore --no-index`: mustTrack must NOT be ignored, mustIgnore must be.
packageScripts  package.json is per-branch; these npm scripts must read exactly this.
A path listed NOWHERE is per-branch by default and is not checked at all. Only `perBranch` buys an
existence check, so list a file there when every branch must have one of its own.
ADDING AN ENTRY IS ITSELF A HARNESS CHANGE: make it on the source branch, then run
`node scripts/harness/branch-sync.js --apply` on each other branch. Adding it on a branch is the
one edit the gate is guaranteed not to see, because the manifest in force is the source's.
Procedure and rationale: docs/reference/branches/README.md
